# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)

Diagnosed cand_0002's own trials from `./trajectories/` (33 trials, 11 val tasks). **Exactly 1 imperfect trial exists** (per-trial reward decomposition: reward = (dq−1)/4 − 0.1·softgates):

| task | trial rewards | failing trial | lost points |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| case-030-real-operator-structured-logging (0.92) | 0.75 / 1.0 / 1.0 | t0 | dq 4/5 (no soft gates; internal review 13/14) |

All 32 other trials score 1.0. No ENVIRONMENT faults — every pipeline completed (decompose → review → revise → re-review → re-revise → final review on the failing trial; others converge earlier). Max recoverable ≈ +0.008 val (0.992 → 1.0). This is a "make the good behavior consistent" (flaky) fix: the two passing siblings of the SAME task made the same two judgment calls but recorded them in the artifact shapes the external grader explicitly rewards.

The dq-4 grader named exactly two gaps: "**Why 4, not 5.** The E001 size overage is a real, acknowledged minor gap, and the HLR-7 P1-into-P0 bundling — while defensibly justified here — is exactly the priority-fidelity risk the annotations warn about, and it is not covered by a triage escape."

| rank | cluster | tasks (trials) | shared root cause | tag | change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Justified epic-size overage left as a terminal note — no re-split trigger | case-030 (t0) | E001 is ~1.25–1.5 sprints by the strategy's own effort estimate, above the ~2-week guideline, kept as one logical change. The final internal review's issue is terminal ("noted for planning awareness only") with NO conditional trigger, and review #1 suggested a split (the CI lint rule) that could not bring the epic under the guideline — the revise executed it, E001 stayed above guideline, and the size minor survived to the final artifact. The external grader cited this ("the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked"). Every dq-5 size flag in the corpus carries a concrete conditional re-split trigger: case-030 t2 "the adversarial review records a concrete re-split trigger if the audit exceeds the 75% estimate. This is a defensible trade-off, not a monolith gap"; t1 "consider splitting if the lint rule is extracted"; case-020 t1 "if the campaign outgrows a sprint of effort, split the access/logistics work"; case-019 t1 "consider a journey-axis split if capacity-constrained" | KNOWLEDGE (what a justified overage must record) + STRUCTURE (review must demand the trigger; revise must have a playbook entry for adding it) | WORKED EXAMPLE + review-check recalibration + revise-playbook entry |
| 2 | P1-into-P0 bundling rationale not recorded as an inline Step-4 priority-split analysis in the traceability matrix | case-030 (t0) | HLR-7 (P1) bundled into P0 E001 — correct call per Step 4's tight-coupling clause, but the rationale lived in the "Boundary decisions" prose + a bare-pointer footnote after the matrix ("bundled with P0 work per the tight-coupling rule above"). The dq-5 siblings record it INLINE: t1's matrix row "E001 (bundled) \| Bundled with P0 work: ... same implementation surface, not independently deferrable. Splitting would force two passes over identical call sites" (grader: "the matrix flags it as 'bundled' with a concrete rationale ... the P1 label reflects relative value, not a separately schedulable deliverable"); t2 carries "an explicit Step-4 priority-split analysis" (grader's words). All 8 passing bundling trials in the corpus use the inline-row shape (case-016 ×3, case-029 ×3, case-030 t1/t2) | KNOWLEDGE/CONTRACT (where the analysis must be recorded) | CONTRACT: recording requirement in Step 4 + review mirror-case check + revise playbook entry |
| 3 | Revise-time structural defects when splitting an epic | case-030 (t0) | (a) The revise, executing review #1's split suggestion, wired an `E001 → E004` dependencies edge for the split-out CI lint rule — no DAG rule creates it (Rule 15 same-repo/different-area = parallel; lint-verification coupling is an AC gate); the re-review caught it (12/14 fail) and the re-revise removed it — an avoidable extra review+revise cycle that an LLM reviewer might not always catch. (b) After the split, the summary's Component Mapping kept "All three epics use this canonical name" with four epics — the external grader named it ("Cosmetic slip ... stale text after the review-driven lint-rule split"). The revise playbook's only size entry was "Oversized epic: Split by sub-deliverable" with no wiring or sweep guidance | KNOWLEDGE (playbook gaps) | REVISE-PLAYBOOK entries: split wiring rule + stale-reference sweep |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit)

| cluster | edit class | file | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | WORKED EXAMPLE (decompose) | `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 8a, Health Warnings bullet | When an epic is kept above ~2 weeks as ONE logical change, record a re-split trigger (concrete planning condition for re-splitting) in Health Warnings — converts an unresolved defect into a managed trade-off. Generalizes to any justified overage | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only when an epic exceeds the guideline AND is kept; the dq-5 shape across the corpus |
| 1 | REVIEW-CHECK RECALIBRATION | `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 3 check | Oversized-epic handling: monolith (multiple logical changes) stays a split demand; ONE logical change above guideline → demand a re-split trigger (minor, correction "record a concrete re-split trigger in Health Warnings"), never a terminal note or an un-actionable split suggestion; trigger already present → watch item, not a defect | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only on above-guideline epics; the 4 passing trials with size flags already write trigger-style conditionals; case-029 t0's monolith major is explicitly preserved |
| 1 | REVISE-PLAYBOOK ENTRY | `prompts/revise-agent.md` Epic Boundary issues | "Oversized but one logical change (review asks for a re-split trigger)": do NOT split; add the trigger to Health Warnings + epic Notes | Yes — revise only acts on review issues; fires only on the trigger-demand shape |
| 2 | CONTRACT (recording requirement) | `prompts/decompose-agent.md` Step 4, priority-split bullet | When keeping a lower-priority HLR bundled, record the priority-split analysis INLINE in the traceability matrix row (`bundled` + why not separately schedulable) — the shape all 8 passing bundling trials already produce | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only on kept bundling; passing trials already comply (verified per-trial) |
| 2 | REVIEW MIRROR-CASE CHECK | `prompts/review-agent.md` Criterion 1 check | Justified bundling is correct only with the analysis on the record (row flag, or a bundling note carrying the full rationale); bare pointer/scattered/absent → minor with correction "record the Step-4 priority-split analysis in the matrix row", never a split demand when the HLR shares the surface | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only on multi-priority epics with missing analysis; all passing bundling trials record it (case-018 t2's substantive note is explicitly accepted) |
| 2 | REVISE-PLAYBOOK ENTRY | `prompts/revise-agent.md` Epic Boundary issues | "Missing bundling analysis": add the `bundled` flag + rationale to the matrix row; do not re-split unless genuinely deferrable on a disjoint surface | Yes — revise only acts on review issues |
| 3 | REVISE-PLAYBOOK ENTRY (split wiring) | `prompts/revise-agent.md` Epic Boundary issues | Splitting an epic: wire the new epic's deps per DAG construction rules — same-repo sub-deliverable split is parallel (Rule 15); edge only for builds-against artifacts (Rule 13); enforcement/verification coupling is an AC gate, never an edge | Yes — BOUNDED: fires only when the revise splits; case-029 t0's split edges (gated_by investigation + build-against Service) are exactly what the rule prescribes |
| 3 | REVISE-PLAYBOOK ENTRY (stale sweep) | `prompts/revise-agent.md` Step 3, new item 5 | After epic structure changes, sweep the whole summary for stale structural references (epic counts in prose, Component Mapping, boundary notes) | Yes — fires only when epics were added/removed/merged |

SKILL.md (dispatcher), fetch-agent.md, and `scripts/validate_decomposition.py` deliberately unchanged: no dispatcher/fetch-phase failure exists; the trigger/bundling-analysis requirements are LLM-judgment (not mechanically decidable), so no validator check applies; the validator's `--self-check` still passes (5 checks fire on bad fixture, clean on good).

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the agent now does on those exact inputs)

- **Cluster 1, decompose side** — trace case-030 t0: the summary's Health Warnings already flag the size drivers ("Unconfirmed audit figure: the '75% of log calls embed identity' figure is an SME estimate; the manager-binary epic's audit step will establish the actual count") but stop there, and the boundary-decision prose argues against a split without any trigger. With the edit, the agent writes the trigger into Health Warnings (e.g. "re-split if the audit exceeds the estimated 75% volume") — exactly the sentence the t2 grader quoted when scoring 5 ("the adversarial review records a concrete re-split trigger if the audit exceeds the 75% estimate. This is a defensible trade-off, not a monolith gap"). Blast radius: BOUNDED — fires only on kept above-guideline epics; passing trials' size handling is unchanged or gains the already-rewarded trigger sentence.
- **Cluster 1, review side** — trace case-030 t0 review #1 issue: "E001 is slightly oversized ... consider splitting the CI lint rule or backwards-compatibility validation into a small follow-up epic" — a split that removes ~0.25 sprint from a ~1.5-sprint epic (per the strategy's own effort estimate the review itself quotes) and cannot bring it under the guideline; final review issue: "noted for planning awareness only". With the edit, review #1 instead flags minor with the correction "record a concrete re-split trigger in the summary's Health Warnings" → the unconditional first revise adds it (new playbook entry) → the final review records a managed watch item instead of an unresolved minor → the external grader's stated reason for the 4 ("the size remains above guideline, which the embedded adversarial review also docked") disappears, and the E001→E004 edge churn never happens because the un-actionable split is no longer suggested. Blast radius: BOUNDED — the 4 passing trials with size flags already write conditional triggers in their issues (case-019 t1 "if capacity-constrained", case-020 t1 "if the campaign outgrows a sprint", case-030 t1 "if the lint rule is extracted", t2's audit-exceeds trigger); case-029 t0's E005 monolith major (multiple work streams bundled) is explicitly outside the new rule.
- **Cluster 2, decompose side** — trace case-030 t0 matrix footnote: "HLR-7 (P1) is bundled with P0 work per the tight-coupling rule above" (a bare pointer; the substance lives in the Boundary decisions prose) vs t1's passing row "E001 (bundled) | Bundled with P0 work: `resourceKind` is added to the same log calls being converted for HLR-1 — same implementation surface, not independently deferrable. Splitting would force two passes over identical call sites". With the edit, t0's agent writes the t1-shaped row; the grader's half-gap ("the annotation's watch-item ... keeps the P1 enhancement non-deferrable") is answered by the recorded not-separately-schedulable analysis the t1/t2 graders quoted when scoring 5. Blast radius: BOUNDED — verified per-trial that every passing bundling decomposition already records the inline flag (case-016 t0/t1/t2, case-029 t0/t1/t2, case-030 t1/t2); tasks without multi-priority epics are untouched.
- **Cluster 2, review side** — trace case-030 t0: the internal review never engaged the HLR-7 bundling (issues were size + the edge only); the external grader did. With the edit, the FIRST review (whose issues the unconditional revise must fix) flags the missing analysis as minor with the "record it" correction, so the analysis lands in the matrix row before the final review. Blast radius: BOUNDED — the check accepts a row flag OR a bundling note carrying the full rationale (case-018 t2's substantive note passes); it fires only when neither exists, which in the corpus is exactly the failing trial's shape.
- **Cluster 3a (split wiring)** — trace case-030 t0 re-review issue: "Edge RHAISTRAT-8010-E001 -> RHAISTRAT-8010-E004 is an unjustified blocking edge that serializes naturally-parallel work. No DAG rule creates it ... the codebase is the rule verification target — an AC-gate coupling per the Rule 10/13 pattern, never a dependencies edge". With the edit, the revise that executes a split wires E004 with no edge to E001 (same repo, different area — Rule 15 parallel; the lint-enforcement coupling becomes E004's AC, which it already carries) — the shape the re-review demanded, without burning the extra review+revise cycle. Blast radius: BOUNDED — fires only when the revise splits an epic; case-029 t0's split (E007 gated_by the design Investigation + depending on E005's rendered Service surface — a builds-against artifact) is exactly what the rule prescribes, so its outcome is unchanged.
- **Cluster 3b (stale sweep)** — trace case-030 t0 external grader: "Cosmetic slip: the summary's Component Mapping says 'all three epics' where there are four — stale text after the review-driven lint-rule split; not structural". With the edit, the revise sweeps the summary after the split and updates the count. Blast radius: BOUNDED — fires only when epic structure changes during revise.

## Process & features used

- Serial this iteration (no subagents/worktrees): exactly one imperfect trial of 33 exists, and all three clusters come from that single trace — one coherent diagnosis chain (per-trial reward decomposition → grader-rationale extraction → t0-vs-t1/t2 artifact diff → corpus-wide blast-radius scan of every size flag and bundling mention). The 7 edits land in 3 prompt files whose contents must stay mutually consistent (decompose Step 4/8a ↔ review Criterion 1/3 ↔ revise playbook); parallel edit-subagents would have conflicted.
- Read in full: `guidance/skill-package/SKILL.md` (levers used: body knowledge note with worked example, contract clarification at the point of use, review-to-revise issue mapping, playbook entries — no new script: the trigger/analysis rules are LLM-judgment, not mechanically decidable), `guidance/diagnose/SKILL.md` (flaky-vs-failing separation — find what the passing trials do and make it reliable; blast-radius naming; near-miss as the cheapest marginal gain).
- Prior iterations read: `prior_iterations/cand_0001/` + `prior_iterations/cand_0002/` (PROCESS.md + diff.patch). Built on cand_0002's accepted review-calibration pattern (discriminating condition + first-review firing + unconditional-revise wiring) — this iteration applies the same wiring to two NEW checks (size-trigger, bundling-analysis).
- Improvement types applied (multiple): worked example (Health Warnings trigger), output-contract clarification at the point of use (Step 4 matrix-row recording), decision-rule narrowing via discriminating condition (monolith vs one-logical-change; recorded vs bare-pointer bundling), review-to-revise issue mapping (Criterion 1/3 checks with named corrections), revise-playbook correction entries (3 new).
- `rejected.jsonl` is empty — no refuted approaches to avoid; `history.jsonl` confirms both prior candidates were ACCEPTED, so nothing needed redesign.

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)

- The discriminator in Criterion 3's new text: monolith (multiple logical changes/work streams) = split demand; ONE logical change above guideline = trigger demand. Broadening the trigger path to monoliths would regress case-029 t0's correct major.
- The discriminator in Criterion 1's new text: the review accepts a row flag OR a substantive bundling note (case-018 t2's shape) and flags only the bare-pointer/absent shape (case-030 t0's). Tightening it to row-flag-only would churn a passing task for no gain; loosening it to "any mention" would not fix the failure.
- The decompose-side Step 4 requirement stays "inline in the matrix row" (the strongest, grader-quoted shape) even though the review tolerates the substantive note — decompose should produce the best shape, review should only catch its absence.
- All of cand_0001/cand_0002's accepted machinery (validator + Step 8c precondition + review 1.7 + revise wiring; the narrow architecture_claims and soft-AC discriminating conditions) is untouched.

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why)

- The t0 grader's positive notes (HLR-1 measurement split, DAG non-edge justifications, SME-override handling) — praised, not gaps: fails the REAL test.
- The t0 grader's "Why not 3" paragraph enumerates what was already handled well — no action.
- A general ~2-week epic-size guideline in the DECOMPOSE prompt — rejected as UNBOUNDED: it could make the decompose agent preemptively split near-limit epics on passing tasks (case-019 t1's E003 "near the ~2-week epic limit; defensible") where the current behavior scores 1.0; the trigger requirement is scoped to the keep-bundled case only.
- A validator check for the trigger/bundling-analysis — not mechanically decidable (requires judging "one logical change" and "same surface"); forcing a keyword check would fire on passing shapes.
- SKILL.md frontmatter/description edits — the runner invokes the skill directly; triggering is not a failure mode.
- mandated-AC (Rules 24/25) validator extension — still staged thresholdless (B9), not REAL (unchanged from cand_0002's assessment).

## Environment faults

None. All 33 trials ran to completion; the single failure is a capability failure (dq 4 on one trial).
